name: motionboard
description: Make product launch films from 38 Apple/Linear-style shot recipes.
readme:
**English** | [简体中文](README_CN.md)

# Motionboard

Shot language from Apple and Linear launch films, rebuilt in code for your agent.

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Claude Code skill](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20Code-skill-d97757)](#install)
[![Codex skill](https://img.shields.io/badge/Codex-skill-111111)](#install)

[motionboard.app](https://motionboard.app) · [All recipes](https://motionboard.app/#recipes)

[![The Motionboard launch film, built from six recipes](assets/readme/film.gif)](https://motionboard.app)

Motionboard breaks real launch films down into 38 shots. Each shot is recreated in code as a ~10 second [HyperFrames](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes) film (HTML and GSAP rendered to video), and the website shows every original next to its recreation. The skill gives your agent all 38 recipes, so it can make one shot or plan and build a whole launch film for your product.

Requirements: Node 22+, HyperFrames (`npx hyperframes`), ffmpeg.

## Install

```sh
npx skills add krisyangdev/motionboard
```

Or hand the link to your agent:

> Install this skill: https://github.com/krisyangdev/motionboard

Agents installing for a user: run `npx skills add krisyangdev/motionboard -g -y` (global, no prompts). If the skill is not available in the current session yet, read `SKILL.md` at the path the command prints (usually `~/.agents/skills/motionboard/`) and follow it.

In Claude Code, add it as a plugin:

```sh
/plugin marketplace add krisyangdev/motionboard
/plugin install motionboard@motionboard
```

Manual install for Claude Code and Codex:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/krisyangdev/motionboard.git ~/motionboard
ln -s ~/motionboard/skills/motionboard ~/.claude/skills/motionboard
ln -s ~/motionboard/skills/motionboard ~/.codex/skills/motionboard
```

## Use

| Say | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Make a launch film for my product with Motionboard. | The agent reads your product, proposes a 4 to 6 shot storyboard with preview links, waits for your OK, builds each shot and joins them into one MP4. |
| Use the match-cut recipe to go from my logo to the app. | The agent builds that one shot with your brand and UI, renders it, and checks it against the preview. |
| Make the Tilted UI with Depth of Field shot for this landing page. | The agent ports the recipe's GSAP timeline into your site as a hero animation. |

Each recipe page on [motionboard.app](https://motionboard.app) has a copy button that gives your agent one line: install this skill, then make that shot.

## Recipes

38 recipes, grouped by where they sit in a launch film.

<!-- recipes:start -->

### Opening (7)

| Recipe | Shot |
| --- | --- |
| [Light Reveal](https://motionboard.app/recipes/light-reveal/) | The product emerges from pure black as exposure rises, with a barely perceptible push-in, and the closing shot runs the same move in reverse. |
| [Showcase Wall](https://motionboard.app/recipes/showcase-wall/) | A full-screen wall of work cards drifts diagonally at constant speed while slowly scaling up, then accelerates into one card at the end. |
| [Word-by-Word Highlight](https://motionboard.app/recipes/word-by-word-highlight/) | Words in a small centered line brighten from gray to white one at a time, and the text never moves. |
| [Rhythmic Typing](https://motionboard.app/recipes/rhythmic-typing/) | Monospace text is typed character by character with a cursor at uneven human speed, then deleted and retyped. |
| [Branching Growth](https://motionboard.app/recipes/branching-growth/) | A single dot branches layer by layer into a network, slow at first and then faster, or splits in doubling beats until it fills the frame. |
| [Iris Window Montage](https://motionboard.app/recipes/iris-window-montage/) | A fixed circular window cuts rapidly between images, or revisits the same image, while its size jumps with the rhythm. |
| [Line Boil](https://motionboard.app/recipes/line-boil/) | Hand-drawn outlines swap to a slightly different trace every few frames, and motion steps at a low frame rate with no tweening. |

### Product reveal (7)

| Recipe | Shot |
| --- | --- |
| [Device Push-in Focus](https://motionboard.app/recipes/device-push-in-focus/) | A line-art 3D laptop turns upright while closed, opens, pushes in on the keyboard, then pans from key to key in step with the option selected in the UI beside it. |
| [Macro Pull-out Reveal](https://motionboard.app/recipes/macro-pull-out-reveal/) | The camera drifts slowly across a surface at extreme close range, then one pull-back reveals the whole device or page. |
| [X-ray Dissolve](https://motionboard.app/recipes/x-ray-dissolve/) | The internal structure and the outer shell cross-dissolve from the same camera position, then the camera pulls back to the whole device. |
| [Text–Object Interleave](https://motionboard.app/recipes/text-object-interleave/) | Text and object interleave in depth: type rises from behind the product, a device slots into a gap in a sentence, or a word passes through an object and comes out as another word. |
| [Outline to Solid](https://motionboard.app/recipes/outline-to-solid/) | A wireframe or light-drawn outline appears first, then fills into a solid shape or material. |
| [Tilted UI with Depth of Field](https://motionboard.app/recipes/tilted-ui-with-depth-of-field/) | A UI plane tilted 10–15° and shot up close, with only the active row in focus and the rest blurred. |
| [Dock Arrival](https://motionboard.app/recipes/dock-arrival/) | A magnified Dock opens a gap, a new icon grows into it with one small spark, and a cursor click opens the window. |

### Features (15)

| Recipe | Shot |
| --- | --- |
| [Dispense Line-up](https://motionboard.app/recipes/dispense-line-up/) | Accessories slide out of the main object one by one into a row while the caption appears word by word, then retract in mirror order. |
| [Auto Zoom / Zoom-to-Cursor](https://motionboard.app/recipes/auto-zoom/) | The camera pushes to the target element in 0.4–0.8s, holds for one click or input, then pulls back to the full view. |
| [Morph Relay](https://motionboard.app/recipes/morph-relay/) | One element keeps morphing into the next, replacing cuts, so the whole sequence has no hard cut. |
| [Wireframe Re-layout](https://motionboard.app/recipes/wireframe-re-layout/) | Content fades to wireframes, the wireframes re-flow into a new layout, then each cell fills with new content in turn. |
| [Card Flip to Code](https://motionboard.app/recipes/card-flip-to-code/) | The preview card rotates 180° around the Y axis and its back face shows the code. |
| [Control-Driven Change](https://motionboard.app/recipes/control-driven-change/) | The frame a control (color picker, toggle, dial) lands, the page result changes on that same frame. It can be split-screen with the control on the left and the result on the right. |
| [Multiplayer Cursors](https://motionboard.app/recipes/multiplayer-cursors/) | Enlarged two-color named cursors move across a canvas, leave comments, and drag items to reorder. |
| [Focus Hop](https://motionboard.app/recipes/focus-hop/) | A highlight block or focus frame hops one cell at a time with the cursor, and the frame can take the color of the icon inside it. |
| [Pile-up and Clear](https://motionboard.app/recipes/pile-up-and-clear/) | Tasks, tags, or events pile up one by one until the screen is full, then clear in one step to a single result state. |
| [Prompt Carousel](https://motionboard.app/recipes/prompt-carousel/) | A line under the headline thickens into a pill, becomes an input box, and types a list of prompts that scroll vertically. |
| [Scattered Spec Type](https://motionboard.app/recipes/scattered-spec-type/) | A spec line is split into words placed far apart on uneven baselines, with a connector word stepping up letter by letter. |
| [Glass Lens](https://motionboard.app/recipes/glass-lens/) | A transparent glass disc, loupe, or control moves over content, magnifying and refracting what lies beneath, with dispersion at the edge. |
| [Map Pin Drop](https://motionboard.app/recipes/map-pin-drop/) | A pin drops onto a map with a bounce and bursts into fragments, the map zooms out to the whole country, and a route line draws to the next city. |
| [Dot-Matrix Glyph](https://motionboard.app/recipes/dot-matrix-glyph/) | A graphic is quantized onto a circular dot-matrix display, and every frame of its rotation or change snaps to the dot grid. |
| [Confirmation Burst](https://motionboard.app/recipes/confirmation-burst/) | On the frame of a tap, payment, or confirmation, lines, squares, and dots radiate from the contact point, or an icon pops with a bounce and an echo outline expands. |

### Transitions (5)

| Recipe | Shot |
| --- | --- |
| [Locked-Layout Reskin](https://motionboard.app/recipes/locked-layout-reskin/) | Layout positions stay locked while the color scheme and fonts hard-cut every 6–10 frames. |
| [Glass Droplet Split](https://motionboard.app/recipes/glass-droplet-split/) | A glass slab stretches into a droplet, its neck thins and breaks, leaving a round bead. A dispersive glass ring contracting inward is the sibling form. |
| [Domino Wave](https://motionboard.app/recipes/domino-wave/) | A row of cubes flips 90 degrees one after another with a phase offset, while the camera pans along the line. |
| [Match Cut](https://motionboard.app/recipes/match-cut/) | One object is replaced by another at the same anchor point, so the viewer's gaze never moves. |
| [Foreground Wipe & Flash](https://motionboard.app/recipes/foreground-wipe-flash/) | A defocused foreground object sweeps across and covers the frame to cut scenes, or a central glow blows out to white before the next scene. |

### Ending (4)

| Recipe | Shot |
| --- | --- |
| [Rotate to Lockup](https://motionboard.app/recipes/rotate-to-lockup/) | An object spins with a long ease-out and stops at the exact angle that forms the logo silhouette or the hero view of the product. |
| [Converge to Mark](https://motionboard.app/recipes/converge-to-mark/) | At the end, multiple elements gather and compress into a single icon or logo, always centered in the frame. |
| [Mark-to-Wordmark Unfold](https://motionboard.app/recipes/mark-to-wordmark-unfold/) | A logo mark sits centered, then the wordmark unfolds from behind it or outward from its center, optionally with a scramble-then-lock effect. |
| [Chromatic Stretch](https://motionboard.app/recipes/chromatic-stretch/) | Some letters of a wordmark stretch horizontally with RGB ghosting, distort in steps, then snap back clean. |

<!-- recipes:end -->

## Website

The site is TanStack Start prerendered to static HTML and served from Cloudflare Workers.

```sh
npm install
npm run dev        # http://127.0.0.1:3000
npm run build      # generate recipe files, prerender every page, write sitemap.xml
npm run deploy     # build, then cf deploy
```

`scripts/recipes.mjs` runs before each dev and build. It writes the agent-facing recipe files for the website (`public/r/`) and for the skill (`skills/motionboard/recipes/`) from `src/data/`, and copies `skills/motionboard/source/` to `public/source/`.

Films and posters are served from R2 at https://media.motionboard.app. Keep source files in `media/` (not tracked) and upload with `scripts/upload-media.sh [file ...]`. Copy, like and wish counts live in D1; apply the schema locally once with `npx wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --local`.

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). The recreations in `skills/motionboard/source/` are original work. The original films belong to their owners and appear on the website only as short reference clips next to the recreations. See [NOTICE](NOTICE).

skillMd:
---
name: motionboard
license: MIT
description: Make product launch films and single shots in the style of Apple and Linear launch films, from 38 recipes (HyperFrames, HTML + GSAP rendered to MP4). Use when the user asks for a product launch film, promo video, product reveal, feature video or app trailer; wants to recreate a specific shot from a launch film; asks for Apple-style or Linear-style motion, either as a video or as a hero animation on a website; or names a shot from the recipe index (Match Cut, Tilted UI with Depth of Field, Auto Zoom, Morph Relay, Light Reveal and the rest). Also applies to requests in Chinese such as 做宣传片, 产品发布视频, 苹果风动效, 复刻某个镜头.
---

# Motionboard

Motionboard is shot language broken down from real Apple and Linear launch films. Each shot is recreated in code as a ~10s HyperFrames film (HTML + GSAP rendered to video). This skill holds 38 recipes and their runnable source projects. You make one shot, or plan and build a whole launch film, for the user's product.

Reply in the user's language. The files here are in English.

## Quality bar

Every shot must reach the finish of its preview film on https://motionboard.app. The preview is the reference. Match its timing, easing, camera, blur, depth, lighting and UI density. A shot that moves correctly but looks flatter, emptier or cheaper than the preview is not finished.

## Layout

- `recipes/index.md`: all recipes grouped by position in a launch film, one line each. Scan this to pick shots.
- `recipes/<slug>.md`: one recipe. Spec table, why it works, the prompt, "matches requests like" phrases, the preview and recipe page links.
- `source/<video>/`: the runnable HyperFrames project for the recipe (`index.html`, `package.json`, `hyperframes.json`). The `Source files` section of each recipe names the folder.

Each recipe page at `https://motionboard.app/recipes/<slug>/` shows the preview film next to the original it was recreated from. Preview film: `https://media.motionboard.app/<video>.mp4`.

Positions: Opening (`open`), Product reveal (`reveal`), Features (`feature`), Transitions (`bridge`), Ending (`close`).

The source folder name can differ from the recipe slug (`auto-zoom` uses `source/zoom-to-cursor/`). Take it from the recipe's `Source files` section.

### Spec, source and preview

- The source project is the shot, and the preview film is its render.
- The spec table and the prompt are taken from the source: its beat times, durations, eases, angles, blur and stagger. Use the Timing row as the beat list for the quality check.
- The timeline in `index.html` is the final word on any detail the table leaves out.

## 1. Setup check

Run once per session before building.

```sh
node --version                  # 22 or newer
npx --yes hyperframes@<version from the recipe's package.json> --version
ffmpeg -version | head -1
```

If one is missing, tell the user what to install and stop. Each source project pins its HyperFrames version in `package.json`, and its scripts are the commands to use:

```sh
npm run dev                          # preview in the HyperFrames studio
npm run check                        # lint, runtime, layout and contrast gate, about a minute
npm run render -- --quality draft    # MP4 into renders/<project>_<timestamp>.mp4
npm run render -- --quality delivery # the final
```

Equivalent: `npx --yes hyperframes@<version> preview | check | render`. `npx --yes hyperframes@<version> snapshot --at <seconds,...> --against <preview.mp4>` writes frames of the composition and a side-by-side sheet against the preview. If the user's agent has the `hyperframes` skills, use them for anything beyond these commands. The "skills out of date" notice HyperFrames prints can be ignored.

Check, render and the quality check need network access: HyperFrames fetches Google Fonts (Inter and others) and GSAP from a CDN, and the preview film downloads from `media.motionboard.app`.

Network use, all of it on the user's machine: `npx --yes hyperframes@<version>` downloads the HyperFrames CLI from npm, `npm install` fetches the project's dependencies, HyperFrames fetches fonts and GSAP at render time, and the quality check downloads one preview MP4 from `media.motionboard.app`. The skill runs no other network calls, no telemetry and no background processes.

### Reading `npm run check`

Run it once on the untouched copy before editing. Some sources already report errors there, on purpose: dim text in blurred depth-of-field layers fails the contrast gate, and clamped rows report `clipped_text`. Then:

- Fix every error your edits add.
- An error already in the untouched copy can stay when it is part of the look. Mark intentional truncation with `data-layout-allow-overflow` and intentional overlap with `data-layout-allow-occlusion`.
- `text_below_floor`, `line_unread` and similar warnings are normal for product UI at real density. Keep type at the preview's size.

Every composition is one `index.html`: a root `data-composition-id="main"` with `data-duration`, 1920x1080, one paused GSAP timeline on `window.__timelines["main"]`. Keep that contract, because the renderer seeks the timeline frame by frame.

## 2. Mode A: one shot

Use when the user wants one shot, or names a recipe.

1. **Find the recipe.** By name or slug: open `recipes/<slug>.md`. By description: match it against `recipes/index.md` and the "Matches requests like" phrases in the likely recipes; read two or three candidates and choose. If two fit, name both in one sentence and let the user pick. Ask nothing else when the choice is clear.
2. **Know the product.** From the user's repo or message: name, logo, brand colours, fonts, real UI. Ask once for what is missing and cannot be read from the repo.
3. **Pick the output.** A video by default. Website motion (section 4) when the user mentions their site or a hero animation.
4. **Read the whole recipe file**, then the whole `source/<video>/index.html`.
5. **Copy the project** and run `npm run check` on the untouched copy. `cp -R <skill dir>/source/<video> <user folder>/<video>`. Never edit files inside the skill folder.
6. **Adapt two layers only.**
   - Brand layer: names, copy, colours, logo, fonts. Replace directly. Keep text inside its boxes after the swap.
   - UI layer: the product screens, cards, windows and controls in the shot. Rebuild the user's real UI in HTML/CSS, from their components and tokens or from screenshots used as reference only. Follow how the source project builds its UI. When the product has no UI like the source's (a launcher, a calendar), map the same flow onto the product's closest real screen.
   - Motion layer: timing, easing, camera moves, layering, stagger, frame counts. Keep exactly as in the source. Change a motion value only when the product forces it (for example a longer word), and record the change.
   - The layers are bound together. The timeline targets elements by id and class, camera moves land on fixed coordinates, and typing and list beats depend on text length and row count. Keep the ids the timeline uses, keep row counts and text lengths close to the source, and when the layout moves, update the target coordinates without changing the times. An interaction the product lacks (a drag in a calendar) becomes the product's own interaction at the same beat time.
   - Some sources open with a lead-in before the recipe's moment (a UI push-in before a logo ending). Keep it in a whole film. When the user asks for only that moment, cut the lead-in, start on the recipe's first beat, and keep every later beat's spacing.
7. **Fonts.** Use the user's brand font when it can be bundled (`@font-face` with a file in the project). For a system font that cannot ship, such as SF Pro, use Inter, which HyperFrames fetches on its own. Some sources use macOS local fonts (PingFang, Songti via `local()`); swap those the same way.
8. `npm run check` (section 1), render, then run the quality check below.

## 3. Mode B: whole launch film

Use when the user wants a launch film, promo, trailer or feature video.

1. **Product.** If there is no link, repo or description, ask for one once. Read the repo or page to learn what the product does, its name, brand, real screens and strongest claims.
2. **Storyboard.** Propose 4 to 6 shots in position order: one Opening, one Product reveal, one to three Features, optionally one Transition, one Ending. Choose from `recipes/index.md`; a recipe fits when its mechanism shows something true about this product. Show a table:

   | Shot | Recipe | What it shows for this product | Seconds | Preview |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

   Preview is the recipe page link. Use each shot's duration from the recipe's film length, trimmed with the user's agreement if the film should be shorter. Pacing reference: the Motionboard launch film on https://motionboard.app is 6 shots in 15.8 seconds. Wait for the user's confirmation or changes. Do not build before that.
3. **Build each shot** as in Mode A, one folder per shot: `launch-film/shots/01-<slug>/`, `02-<slug>/`, and so on. Keep brand, colours and type identical across shots. Run the quality check on every shot.
4. **Join** the renders with hard cuts, or with the Transition recipe as its own shot between two others. Re-encode so the parts match:

   ```sh
   # list.txt: one line per shot, with each shot's final render, e.g.
   # file 'shots/01-rhythmic-typing/renders/rhythmic-typing_2026-10-30_10-00-00.mp4'
   ffmpeg -f concat -safe 0 -i list.txt -c:v libx264 -crf 14 -pix_fmt yuv420p -an launch-film.mp4
   ```

   Add music only when the user asks.
5. **Deliver** `launch-film.mp4` and the editable project folder (all shot folders plus `list.txt`). Report the quality-check notes per shot.

## 4. Website motion

The same recipe can be a hero animation on a website. Do it when the user asks. Port the GSAP timeline in the source `index.html` into the user's stack (React, Vue, Svelte, plain HTML). Build the same DOM, keep durations, delays and easings, start it when the element scrolls into view, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` by showing the final frame as a static state.

## 5. Quality check before delivering

1. Render the project.
2. Download the preview film (`https://media.motionboard.app/<video>.mp4`) and capture the same moments from both:

   ```sh
   curl -o preview.mp4 https://media.motionboard.app/<video>.mp4
   npx --yes hyperframes@<version> snapshot --at 0.5,2.4,4.0,6.3,9.5 --against preview.mp4
   ```

   Use the beat times from the spec table's Timing row: start, the moment each phase begins, the peak of the move, the hold, the end. When you cut a lead-in, the preview's times are later by the length you cut: take those frames with `ffmpeg -ss <t> -i preview.mp4 -frames:v 1 ref-<t>.png` and compare them with `snapshot --at` frames of your render.
3. Compare each pair. Fix differences in timing, easing, blur, depth of field, shadows, lighting, scale and density. The frames should match beat for beat; only brand and UI content differ.
4. Deliver with a short list of the parameters that were changed for the product and why.

## 6. No placeholder UI

Never ship grey boxes, lorem ipsum, stock icons standing in for real ones, or a pasted screenshot. Product UI is rebuilt in code at the density of the source project: real-looking copy, icons, avatars, data, states, hairline borders, shadows. If the user's product has no UI yet, design a believable one from its description, at the same density as the source.

## 7. Boundaries

- The skill ships recreations only. Do not download or embed the original third-party films. The recipe pages link to YouTube for the originals.
- Recipes and source files are free to use in the user's own work, including commercial launch films.
